System description:
# Case: Tesla Model X with Autopilot (Mountain View, California, 2018)

Source: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-20/01. This is a description of the system and its use before the crash. It does not include the investigation findings.

## System
A 2017 Tesla Model X has Autopilot, a SAE Level 2 partial driving automation feature. It combines Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) and Autosteer (lane keeping). The driver stays responsible for driving and monitoring the road.

## Main parts
- Sensors: a forward-facing camera, a forward-facing radar and ultrasonic sensors.
- Vision processing: a camera-based system detects lane markings, vehicles and some objects ahead.
- TACC: holds a speed set by the driver, follows a vehicle ahead at a chosen gap, and returns to the set speed when no vehicle is ahead.
- Autosteer: keeps the vehicle in its lane using lane markings and the path of the vehicle ahead.
- Forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking are available as separate features.
- Driver monitoring: steering torque is used to check that the driver's hands are on the wheel, with visual and audible alerts if no hands are detected for a period of time.

## People
- The driver sets the cruising speed, turns Autopilot on, and is told to keep hands on the wheel and watch the road.
- Other road users and road workers share the highway. Road agencies maintain road markings and safety hardware such as barriers and crash attenuators.

## Operating context
Busy multi-lane freeway with high-occupancy-vehicle (HOV) lanes, exits and interchanges, lane markings of different quality, and traffic that changes in speed.

requirements.text: The system shall monitor driver attention independently of steering torque and, when the driver is not attending to the road while Autopilot is active, issue an escalating alert and disengage Autopilot if attention is not restored.

When vision processing detects a stationary object in the vehicle's path but cannot classify it confidently, the system shall treat it as a potential hazard, inhibit acceleration toward it, and warn the driver or apply braking as required to avoid a collision.

TACC shall not resume the set speed solely because a lead vehicle is no longer tracked; it shall resume only when available sensor data indicates that the vehicle's path is clear, and shall inhibit acceleration and alert the driver when clearance is uncertain.

When lane markings or the path of a vehicle ahead provide conflicting or ambiguous guidance at a lane transition, Autosteer shall not steer into the indicated path; it shall alert the driver and relinquish lateral control.

When available sensor data indicates an imminent collision with an object in the vehicle's path, automatic emergency braking shall apply sufficient braking to mitigate or avoid the collision, including when object classification confidence is low.

The driver-monitoring system shall not count steering torque alone as confirmation that the driver is holding the wheel; it shall require an independent indication of active driver contact and issue an alert when that indication is absent.

When traffic or roadside equipment occludes a region into which a pedestrian or road worker could enter the vehicle's path, the system shall warn the driver and limit vehicle speed to the configured safe speed for that occlusion until the region is observable or the vehicle has passed it.

When lane markings are detected as faded, conflicting, or insufficient to determine a reliable lane path, Autosteer shall alert the driver and disable lane keeping until reliable lane guidance is available.

When another vehicle enters the selected following gap, TACC shall detect the cut-in and adjust speed promptly enough to maintain the configured minimum safe following distance, or warn the driver if that distance cannot be maintained.

The road agency shall inspect barriers and crash attenuators at locations where roadway design relies on them, and shall repair or replace missing or damaged hardware before reopening the affected location to traffic.
